outcome: Maternal hemostatic alterations (measured by ROTEM and CCTs)
Neonatal hemostatic alterations (measured by ROTEM and CCTs)
cohort: The study included 31 pregnant women with preeclampsia (34 newborns) and 45 pregnant women without preeclampsia (47 newborns).
finding: ROTEM identified maternal hypercoagulability with hyperfibrinolysis and neonatal hypocoagulability during the first hour of life in women with preeclampsia and their offspring, with several alterations not reflected in conventional coagulation tests.
cross-section timing: Maternal blood collected intrapartum; neonatal arterial samples obtained within the first hour of life.
